description: `minimumReleaseAge` must match web/pnpm-workspace.yaml's: pnpm's `minimumReleaseAgeStrict` refuses a younger release, leaving the PR with a stale lock file.
`dependencyDashboardApproval`, not `prCreation: "approval"`, which creates branches without PRs until they fill `branchConcurrentLimit`.
`platformAutomerge` waits only for the `main` ruleset's required checks, so every PR-reporting Woodpecker pipeline must stay required there.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: `fix`, not `chore`, so a security update cuts a release (and an image) by itself; they skip dashboard approval, so a person merges them.

customManagers.description: npx tool versions pinned inside agent skill docs, so instructions cannot drift past the pin they document
pnpm installed in CI steps and the web image; must match web/package.json packageManager.
Dev and test mail images (scripts/images.sh); keep on the same pins as mailroom-mcp.

packageRules.description: Nothing on a PR exercises these (workflows run from `main`), so they never automerge; a group automerges only if every member may.
No mise.lock here, so lock file maintenance has nothing to refresh.
release.yaml runs only on a `v*` tag, so nothing on a PR exercises its images; they never automerge, in a group of their own so the other pipeline images still do.
The soak exists for pnpm (npm-only); a digest update is the same tag rebuilt, usually for a CVE, so it is not held.
Constraints are open `>=`, so upgrades arrive as named PRs touching `uv.lock` alone.
Kept out of the uv group so new diagnostics are attributable to their PR.
`uv lock --upgrade-package` takes no version (renovatebot/renovate#41624), so a soak only fails the run without holding anything back.
`bump`: pnpm 12 refuses `update --no-save` under `minimumReleaseAgeStrict`, so in-range updates would leave a stale lock file.
Each can add lint rules that fail a green branch; fix the new diagnostics in the same PR.
`@vitest/coverage-v8` declares an exact `vitest` peer, so the two move together.
One PR for mise.toml, packageManager, and the CI/Containerfile regex.
`python/cpython` is what mise's entry resolves to; the python3.14 in the uv image tag is not covered.
`astral-sh/uv` is what mise's entry resolves to.
mise/pyenv report release timestamps and docker does not, so a soak would split each group across versions.
One group across compose.yml (dev) and backend-tests.yaml (CI), so tests never run against a Postgres the developer doesn't.
One group across scripts/images.sh and backend-tests.yaml, so CI tests mailroom-core against the same servers as dev; no soak on either side, as for the other docker images.
